rules.name: remote network-to-shell separation
rules.requirement: Network-retrieved content MUST be materialized and pass immutable identity, integrity, provenance and policy admission before shell execution; direct curl/wget-to-eval/sh transitions are forbidden on the canonical production path.

rules.name: immutable executable identity
rules.requirement: Floating branch names, including X, MUST NOT constitute production executable identity or promotion evidence; a full immutable commit/artifact identity is required.

rules.name: no transitive trust from curation
rules.requirement: X-CMD package curation MUST NOT be interpreted as FA3 artifact trust; each executable package requires independent integrity, provenance, licence and admission evidence.

rules.name: capability-mediated agent shell
rules.requirement: Agent access to x-cmd or any shell/tool surface MUST carry caller identity, workspace scope, explicit capability scope and authoritative policy/tool-mediation approval.

rules.name: project instructions are scoped context
rules.requirement: Agent instruction files, injected prompts and skill metadata are untrusted scoped context and MUST NOT grant policy, identity, secret, network, host-resource or execution authority.

rules.name: self-update is not production authority
rules.requirement: Provider self-update or floating upgrade commands MUST NOT mutate a production runtime without explicit external change authorization, immutable target identity and post-change evidence.

rules.name: global host mutation externally authorized
rules.requirement: Any host-global package, PATH, shell-startup or filesystem mutation requires explicit external authorization and auditable change evidence; provider convenience commands do not constitute that authority.

rules.name: cross-cutting authority boundaries preserved
rules.requirement: X-CMD modules for AI, network, packages or agents MUST NOT bypass FA3 MCP/tool mediation, model routing, secrets, egress, host-resource, artifact-trust, workflow or evidence authorities.

rules.name: on-demand does not imply hidden background authority
rules.requirement: Lazy tool materialization may occur only after an admitted invocation; undeclared background fetch, polling or prefetch is forbidden for an inactive optional provider.

rules.name: disabled provider near-zero runtime cost
rules.requirement: When disabled/reference-only, X-CMD MUST require no resident provider process, background worker, network session, accelerator reservation or active polling.

rules.name: provider non-authority invariant
rules.requirement: FA3-PROVIDER-XCMD-001 remains optional, non-root, non-authoritative, adds no capability and preserves the canonical capability count of 143.

rules.name: attributable execution evidence
rules.requirement: Every material x-cmd/tool execution used by FA3 automation MUST be attributable to caller, request, workspace, capability/policy decision, executable artifact identity and result evidence.
